segments.title: 第17章 滿分作文
segments.content:
Reborn to a Time of Verdant Youth: Chapter 17, A Perfect-Score Essay

Beneath the focused gaze of the entire school, Li Luo rose from his seat.

Even though he possessed a full 35 years of life experience.

This was the first time in two lifetimes, a truly groundbreaking first, that he had gone on stage to receive an award in front of so many watchful eyes.

Li Luo followed behind Ying Chanxi, weaving through the chairs where his classmates were seated. He couldn't help but feel a little nervous and a little excited.

That feeling of adrenaline pumping, causing his arms to go slightly numb and his heart to beat faster, was truly a rare occurrence in Li Luo’s life.

But when he looked ahead at Ying Chanxi's composed stride and calm expression, her figure walking steadily toward the podium, Li Luo couldn't help but marvel.

As expected of Ying Chanxi, who had been collecting awards since childhood until her hands went soft, for whom going on stage to receive awards and give speeches was as common as a daily meal.

His on-the-spot composure, even as a 35-year-old geezer, couldn't match that of a young girl.

It was a bit embarrassing, really.

Thinking this, Li Luo straightened his posture, puffed out his chest, and walked onto the stage with a composed expression.

There were eleven people in total, one more than the number of Outstanding Teachers, but no one paid it any mind.

Once on the stage, the teacher in charge of photos wanted Ying Chanxi to stand in the center.

But Ying Chanxi stopped at the edge of the stage, bent down, and tied her shoelace.

By the time she stood up, the other ten students had already lined up.

So Ying Chanxi very naturally stood at the very end next to Li Luo, and received her award certificate from the principal.

The two of them stood close together, their image captured in the group photo by the teacher taking pictures.

Among these eleven outstanding graduates, there were top-tier students like Ying Chanxi and Liu Shaowen, who had excellent academic records and had won a slew of competition awards.

There were also students who participated in sports, music, painting, and other activities, having won at least provincial-level awards.

In addition, there was a student who had been reported by the local TV station for doing good deeds.

So Li Luo's presence among them didn't seem too abrupt or conspicuous.

"How was the surprise?" Ying Chanxi whispered to Li Luo with a smile as they walked down from the stage.

"It was indeed quite a surprise." Li Luo nodded, still savoring the feeling of looking out at the sea of heads on the sports field just now. It was strangely exhilarating. "My spot was a last-minute addition, right? There were supposed to be only ten."

"Who told you to do so well on the high school entrance exam," Ying Chanxi said with a laugh. "I think you deserve it."

"That's true," Li Luo accepted his childhood friend's praise with a thick-skinned grin, then added, "But I had no idea my essay got a perfect score."

"I'll go find Teacher Zhang after this and ask to see your essay," Ying Chanxi said as they walked. "Your essays used to be just twenty-five or twenty-six points. How did you get such a high score this time? Zhao Rongjun himself has never gotten a perfect score on his own essays. How did he teach you?"

"Maybe I'm just a fast learner," Li Luo said shamelessly. "Inspiration insisted on drilling into my head in the exam hall. I couldn't help it."

Getting a perfect score on a language arts essay was something one could only hope for, not plan for.

During the exam, Li Luo had simply followed the standard argumentative essay format of introduction, body, and conclusion. He copied three anecdotes about famous people that fit the topic from his memory, pairing each with a famous quote.

Then he logically summarized three sub-arguments, which he combined into one main argument to complete his proof.

He added a few pretentious-sounding literary sentences, and an eight-hundred-word high school entrance exam essay was complete.

He had no idea how it got a perfect score.

As he thought this, Li Luo had already followed Ying Chanxi back to their seats.

Zhao Rongjun, who sat behind him, leaned forward, took the award certificate from Li Luo's hand, and examined it with curiosity. "I'm so jealous, I don't have one."

"Be humble, be discreet, there's nothing to see." Li Luo took the certificate back and carefully flattened it on his lap. "I have to show this to my parents when I get home. Don't you dare wrinkle it for me."

Shao Heqi and Jin Yuting, seated in front and behind, could taste the sourness in their mouths upon hearing this.

But Li Luo's score was indeed higher than theirs, so they couldn't say anything and could only stew in their feelings.

Especially Jin Yuting. The thought that she might not meet the cutoff score for No. 1 Affiliated High, while Li Luo had secured a spot, made her cringe.

When she remembered all the taunts she had directed at Li Luo before the exam... my god! It was so embarrassing!

Now Li Luo had even received the title of Outstanding Graduate, and he had earned it fair and square through his own efforts in the exam.

This was like another knife stabbing into Jin Yuting's heart.

It made Jin Yuting too embarrassed to even talk to Li Luo and Ying Chanxi now; she felt it would be strangely awkward.

Fortunately, Li Luo wasn't in the habit of holding grudges against kids. Since Jin Yuting and Shao Heqi weren't talking to him, he certainly couldn't be bothered to go out of his way to rub it in their faces.

Now that he had received the Outstanding Graduate award certificate, the surprise Teacher Zhang mentioned had come to fruition.

As for what the principal said afterward, Li Luo paid no attention. He only snapped out of his daze when the principal finally announced the end of the graduation ceremony.

"It's already four-thirty," Li Luo glanced at Shao Heqi's watch, stood up, and stretched. "Are we going straight to Jiangnan Restaurant later, Vice Monitor?"

"Ah, yes." Shao Heqi's reaction was a bit delayed. He glanced at Li Luo and the award certificate in his hand, then quickly averted his gaze and replied, "We'll move the chairs back to the classroom, and then we can head over. It's only a few hundred meters from the school."

"Then I'll put my award certificate in your schoolbag for a bit," Li Luo turned to Ying Chanxi and said. "Be careful not to crush it. Give it back to me tonight when I get home."

"Got it." Ying Chanxi took the certificate directly from Li Luo's hand, stacked hers on top of his, and then said, "Then I'll leave my chair to you."

Shao Heqi, in front of them, let out a sigh. He picked up his own chair, his retreating figure appearing increasingly desolate as he silently followed the line of people leaving.

Once everyone returned to the classroom and put away their chairs, their homeroom teacher, Zhang Wei, clapped his hands on the lectern to get everyone's attention.

"Let's take a short break, and then we'll line up with the students from Class Six and head to Jiangnan Restaurant together."

"There are a few things I need to make clear to you all in advance. Don't think you can just ignore your teacher's words now that you've graduated."

"You must stay in line on the way there. Be careful when crossing the street, and don't jaywalk."

"Once we're at the restaurant, you're not allowed to drink alcohol, you know that, right? Only soft drinks."

"We still have some class funds left over. Shao Heqi will just need to collect another 30 yuan from each of you."

Actually, thirty yuan per person wasn't quite enough, but Zhang Wei was in high spirits from receiving the Outstanding Teacher award and decided to cover the rest out of his own pocket.

...

"Careful now, put it in slowly."

Before they left, Li Luo stood beside Ying Chanxi, watching her place the award certificates safely into her schoolbag before nodding in satisfaction.

And Ying Chanxi hadn't forgotten to ask Teacher Zhang for Li Luo's perfect-score essay.

"Here, you can have this first." Zhang Wei came back from the office and handed over a photocopy of the essay. He then smiled at Li Luo and said, "I might not be an expert on essays, but yours is really well-written. I thought it was excellent just reading it."

"Ahem, you flatter me, you flatter me." Li Luo took his essay from Teacher Zhang and smoothly tucked it into Ying Chanxi's schoolbag.

After all the students in the class were ready, Zhang Wei called for everyone to leave the classroom and line up in the hallway.

The nearly one hundred students from Class Five and Class Six, along with their subject teachers, headed out of the school in a grand procession.

...

"What are you looking at? Watch your step."

In the line for Class Six, Lin Yuan, who had placed first in his class this time, reminded Hua Xiuxiu, who had placed second, beside him.

Hua Xiuxiu ignored him, her head still lowered in concentration, holding a piece of paper in her hand. On it was a photocopied essay.

The title was "The World's Warmth and Cold, Known Only by the Drinker."

"Like a person drinking water, they alone know if it is cold or warm." Hua Xiuxiu mumbled, pondering the origin of the essay's title. The more she thought about it, the more profound it seemed.

After arriving at school this afternoon, Hua Xiuxiu had asked her homeroom teacher, Teacher Wang, for the several perfect-score essays from this year's high school entrance exam.

To her surprise, one of them was from their own school, written by a student from the class next door named Li Luo.

Hua Xiuxiu had never even heard of this name before, nor had she ever seen him featured in the school's publication of outstanding essays.

This made her extremely curious.

So, during the graduation ceremony in the afternoon, Hua Xiuxiu had already taken the time to secretly read this essay several times.

"Is it really that good?" Lin Yuan, beside her, glanced at Hua Xiuxiu's rather delicate profile and remarked, "Getting a perfect score on an essay is often a matter of luck. Maybe it was just a flash of inspiration in the exam hall. If you asked the person to do it again, they might not be able to write something so good."

"Then how come you haven't had a stroke of luck in three years of middle school?" Hua Xiuxiu glanced at him, her eyes meeting Lin Yuan's. "Skill is skill. Didn't you see at the graduation ceremony just now?"

"That Li Luo from the class next door who wrote this essay, he originally only had a score of over four hundred."

"But in just one month before the exam, he raised his score to 555. That's higher than both of our scores, isn't it?"

"This perfect-score essay of his, which discusses interpersonal relationships, could it be a reflection of his feelings about the relationships around him when his grades were poor?"

"Look at this finishing touch at the end of his essay."

At this point, Hua Xiuxiu's tone shifted, becoming somewhat deeper and more rhythmic as she recited: "Nature's warmth and cold cycle through spring, summer, autumn, and winter, through the blooming and fading of flowers; humanity's warmth and cold see cups raised in cheer at dawn, and lamps dimmed at dusk."

"This line is not just well-written, it also echoes the meteorological bureau's words mentioned in the essay prompt. It's perfectly on topic."

"How could writing a sentence like this during a timed exam be dismissed as mere luck?"

Hua Xiuxiu had always been a literature aficionado. Born into a scholarly family, she was an avid reader.

As the language arts representative, her language scores were among the best in the entire school.

For instance, in this high school entrance exam, the highest language score at Yucai Middle School was 112. Hua Xiuxiu was just one point shy of that, ranking second in the school for that subject.

Li Luo, with 110 points, was third.

Other than them, no one else at Yucai Middle School had a language score above 110.

But for Lin Yuan, this was hard to swallow.

Class Five and Class Six usually had a good relationship, and the boys would often get together to play basketball.

Lin Yuan's height was a sore point; he had always been stuck at around 1.65 meters.

That bastard Li Luo from the class next door always managed to block his shots when guarding him, which made Lin Yuan's blood boil every time.

Fortunately, his own grades were much better than Li Luo's, so he could at least claim a moral victory when he lost on the court.

But this time, that kid Li Luo had staged a massive comeback. His entrance exam score was higher than his own, and he even produced a perfect-score essay.

It drove him crazy that all Hua Xiuxiu could talk about today was Li Luo, Li Luo, Li Luo.

But Li Luo's perfect-score essay was genuinely impressive, and Lin Yuan couldn't find any grounds for criticism, so he could only watch sullenly as Hua Xiuxiu admired it again and again.

It wasn't until they arrived at Jiangnan Restaurant and were seated at the table that Lin Yuan watched Hua Xiuxiu put away the essay in her hand, finally letting him breathe a sigh of relief.

But when the meal was halfway through and everyone was getting up with glasses of juice to toast the teachers, Hua Xiuxiu suddenly stood up and asked Lin Yuan, "Which one over there is Li Luo?"

"Huh?" Lin Yuan was stunned for a moment. He subconsciously pointed in the right direction, only to see Hua Xiuxiu walk straight towards Li Luo with her juice. "Wait, hey... hold on."

Lin Yuan quickly trotted after her.

He then saw Hua Xiuxiu walk up to Li Luo, greet him politely, and then ask, "Excuse me, regarding the essay you wrote for the high school entrance exam, what was your thought process or inspiration at the time?"

The question she asked... Lin Yuan covered his forehead, feeling embarrassed for Hua Xiuxiu.

But that was just the kind of person she was. When it came to anything related to literature, she completely disregarded the opinions of those around her, so Lin Yuan couldn't say much about it.

As for Li Luo, who had been asked the question, he was looking at Hua Xiuxiu with a puzzled expression. Then he replied casually, "It was just good luck, a flash of inspiration. If you asked me to do it again, I might not be able to. It's not worth mentioning."

Even though it was similar to his own earlier dismissal of Li Luo, hearing it from Li Luo's own mouth, Lin Yuan could only think, what a freaking show-off.

If only he were the one who had written that perfect-score essay
